goal: Teach generate-index-md.js and generate-relationships-md.js the disclosed-cap documents: frontmatter stamping that generate-exports-md.js and generate-hotspots-md.js already do, so their foundation docs bind to code in the graph. MEASURED (CODEREF-CORE, 2026-08-01, live graph): 8 of 8 foundation docs ingest as @Doc nodes, but only 2 of 8 (EXPORTS, HOTSPOTS) bear documents edges. INDEX.md and RELATIONSHIPS.md are FULLY MECHANICAL - generated from .coderef/index.json and graph.json - so a documents: claim is assertable for them exactly as it is for EXPORTS/HOTSPOTS; today they emit related_files (20 and 17 entries) but no documents:, and related_files mints NO edge in doc-ingest. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: enhance-existing-docs.js (API/ARCHITECTURE/COMPONENTS/SCHEMA). It deliberately refuses to stamp documents: - source comment: 'Never a documents: claim - these docs are hand-authored; coverage cannot be asserted'. That refusal is CORRECT and must not be undone; those four are hand-authored prose the enhancer only decorates with UUID anchors and mechanically-derived related_files. Reuse the DOCUMENTS_CAP=20 disclosed-truncation pattern from generate-exports-md.js so a capped list never reads as complete coverage. Expected effect: foundation-doc documents-edge coverage 2/8 -> 4/8, with the remaining 4 correctly unbound by design. SECONDARY (optional, larger): doc-ingest.ts mints edges from documents: only - related_files: is parsed into DocFact.relatedFiles and then never used to mint anything, so 37 related_files entries across INDEX/RELATIONSHIPS/API are inert metadata. Decide whether related_files should mint a weaker edge kind or stay advisory.

tasks.description: Read the WORKING stamping pattern in scripts/doc-gen/generate-exports-md.js (DOCUMENTS_CAP=20, ranked by exported-element count, cap DISCLOSED via documents_truncated) and generate-hotspots-md.js. Then read the two targets, generate-index-md.js and generate-relationships-md.js, to find where each already computes its per-file coverage set. Also read scripts/doc-gen/enhance-existing-docs.js:46-51 to confirm the OUT-OF-SCOPE boundary in the source itself.

BEFORE snapshot: record foundation-doc documents-edge coverage from the live .coderef/graph.json (expected 2 of 8: EXPORTS, HOTSPOTS) plus the full node/edge id fingerprint, so the after-state proves the change is ADDITIVE and touches nothing else.

generate-index-md.js: stamp a capped, DISCLOSED documents: frontmatter list reusing the generate-exports-md.js pattern verbatim (same cap constant, same documents_truncated disclosure key). INDEX.md is fully mechanical (projected from .coderef/index.json), so a coverage claim is assertable. Do NOT drop or reorder its existing related_files.
generate-relationships-md.js: same capped, disclosed documents: stamping. RELATIONSHIPS.md is projected from graph.json + index.json, so its coverage claim is assertable on the same grounds.

Run the 6 doc-gen generators then scripts/doc-gen/validate-docs.js. Validator must exit 0 (the 25 invalid-UUID-anchor warnings are pre-existing, STUB-48QPYN). Confirm INDEX.md and RELATIONSHIPS.md now carry documents: and that EXPORTS/HOTSPOTS are unchanged in shape.

AFTER proof: repopulate .coderef and verify (a) foundation-doc documents-edge coverage is 4 of 8, (b) the 4 enhance-existing-docs docs (API/ARCHITECTURE/COMPONENTS/SCHEMA) STILL carry zero documents: — the deliberate refusal must survive, (c) the non-doc code universe node/edge id sha256 is byte-identical to the P1-T2 before-snapshot, proving the change is confined to the doc lane.
Run __tests__/pipeline/doc-ingest.test.ts (the doc-ingestion contract surface) and confirm counts, not exit codes. Full suite only if doc-ingest surfaces a change.
Commit via the guarded runner (commit-by-path, WO-ID in subject). Stage the two generators plus the regenerated foundation docs only.

Terminal hard stop: finalize communication.json to checkpoint_ready, flip the registry row via the canonical writer, author the session log, write terminal-post-exec.txt. Await operator /close-workorder.
